observable.commitment: The named observable of this gate is a BAO distance ratio at an effective redshift, in one of two forms the release's own table states: the anisotropic pair (D_M/r_d, D_H/r_d) with D_H = c/H(z), or the isotropic D_V/r_d with D_V = (z D_H D_M^2)^(1/3), together with the release's fiducial cosmology (the cosmology and r_d,fid under which its pipeline converted redshifts to distances) and its covariance. The release, its effective redshifts, its values and its covariance are NOT COMMITTED HERE: they are published data, none was fetched, and choosing a release by name from memory would commit numbers this session may not type. The committed form is the contract; the request (externalRequests.O1) names what Carl's session must fetch and record; every leg that needs the table (O1 to O3, F1 to F5's published comparison, the contract's item (e)) is NOT RUN until the file exists. This is a departure from the prompt's 'which release, which effective redshift' wording, recorded here before any run (decision DEC1 below).

forms.anisotropic: D_M(z)/r_d and D_H(z)/r_d at z_eff, a 2 x 2 block per effective redshift (or the release's full block matrix)
forms.fiducialRescale: alpha_perp = [D_M/r_d] / [D_M,fid/r_d,fid], alpha_par = [D_H,fid r_d,fid] / [D_H r_d]; alpha_iso = [D_V/r_d] / [D_V,fid/r_d,fid]. A table that quotes alphas is converted with its own fiducial values; a model is compared with the measurement only through the ratio D/r_d, never through a distance in Mpc alone.

observable.fitModel: flat Lambda-CDM with Or = 0 in the likelihood (the redshifts are below 3, where radiation is below 1 part in 1,000 of E^2; stated), parameters (Om, theta) with theta = c / (H0 r_d) a nuisance, model = theta * b(Om) with b_DM = Int dz/E, b_DH = 1/E, b_DV = (z/E)^(1/3) (Int dz/E)^(2/3), E^2 = Om (1+z)^3 + 1 - Om. The profile over theta is analytic: theta_hat = b^T C^-1 d / (b^T C^-1 b), chi2_prof(Om) = d^T C^-1 d - (b^T C^-1 d)^2 / (b^T C^-1 b). BAO alone gives Om and H0 r_d only; it gives no H0 and no r_d separately and the gate never reads one from it.
observable.intervals: the set {Om in [0.02, 0.98] : chi2_prof(Om) <= min + delta}, delta = 1 (68.27 percent) or 4 (95.45 percent) for one parameter; end points by Brent's method between grid nodes (grid step 0.001); a set that reaches a grid edge is 'open' and is reported as not constrained on that side, never as a number.

soundHorizon.definition: r_s(z_d) = Int_0^{a_d} c_s c da / (a^2 H(a)), c_s = 1/sqrt(3 (1 + R)), R = 3 rho_b / (4 rho_gamma) = (3 omegaB / (4 omegaGamma)) a, a^2 H = H0 sqrt(Om a + Or + Ok a^2 + Ode a^(1 - 3 w)); finite at a = 0; units Mpc. The drag redshift z_d is an INPUT of the integral. No fitting formula for z_d or r_d is implemented by this gate (coefficients are published data; externalRequests.F1).
soundHorizon.radiation: omegaGamma = rho_gamma / rho_crit,100 with rho_gamma = (pi^2/15) (k T)^4 / (hbar c)^3 / c^2 (SI, k, hbar, c the exact defined values; T = 2.7255 K as astropy 6.0.1's Planck18 Tcmb0, read from astropy by the oracle and pinned), rho_crit,100 = 3 (100 km/s/Mpc)^2 / (8 pi G) with G from astropy.constants (CODATA 2018, pinned in the oracle output), Mpc = 3.0856775814913673e22 m; Or h^2 = omegaGamma (1 + (7/8) (4/11)^(4/3) Neff), Neff = 3.046 unless a world says otherwise, massless neutrinos. Massive neutrinos are not modelled; their effect is bracketed in leg P1 and in no other.
soundHorizon.domain: design domain of the integral, stated and not a property of any fitting formula: z_d in [500, 3000]; omegaB > 0 and Ob < Om (Ob = omegaB / h^2); omegaGamma > 0 and Or > 0; the 255 kernel's own domain for H0, Om, Or, Ode, w, as in COSMOLOGY_II.md section 2. Outside it the function refuses with a code and returns no number.
soundHorizon.referenceCosmologies: ten worlds in this file's worlds block: round numbers chosen for the test, claims about nothing in the sky.

worlds.note: Ode 'flat' means Ode = 1 - Om - Or. Or is derived from T and Neff as stated above and passed to the kernel; astropy's Ogamma0 + Onu0 (massless) must agree with it (leg R1).

closedFormSets.note: Lambda-free flat matter + radiation (Ode = 0, Om = 1 - Or) with baryon loading, H0 = 70, z_d = 1060: the integral has the closed form r_s = (c/H0) (1/sqrt(3)) (2 / sqrt(b Om)) [ ln( sqrt(b (Om a_d + Or)) + sqrt(Om (1 + b a_d)) ) - ln( sqrt(b Or) + sqrt(Om) ) ], b = 3 omegaB / (4 omegaGamma), derived in BAO_GATE.md by differentiating the logarithm (the antiderivative of 1/sqrt((b a + 1)(Om a + Or))).

standardRuler.relation: (D_M/r_d)(z) = theta I(z; Om, Ok, w), (D_H/r_d)(z) = theta / E(z), with theta = c/(H0 r_d); D_V = (z D_H D_M^2)^(1/3), equivalently D_V^3 = c z (1+z)^2 D_A^2 / H(z). Scaling (H0, r_d) -> (lambda H0, r_d / lambda) leaves every ratio unchanged. The ratio, never the distance, is the observable; D_M in a curved world is the transverse comoving distance of the 255 kernel.
standardRuler.tables: Prompt 255's kernel (js/kernels/cosmology/late) supplies D_M and E; the gate's G legs compare its D_M, D_H and D_V with closed forms and with astropy 6.0.1.

combination.rule: A joint constraint from independent measurements is the PRODUCT of their likelihoods on a common parameter grid, i.e. the SUM of their chi-squares, and nothing else: chi2_joint(p) = chi2_BAO(p) + chi2_other(p) with a nuisance profiled per factor only when it is not shared. The factors must be statistically independent (a stated assumption of the user of the rule); the rule never adds an uncertainty, never averages a best fit and never reads a joint contour from two marginal intervals.
combination.with256: OMITTED. Prompt 256's committed verdict (SN_LIKELIHOOD_GATE.md section 10.5) is FC, and Appendix C's entry for 256 C removes '257's combination' (and 260's supernova step). No supernova likelihood, no contour of 256's prototype and no split-form or diagonal covariance is used here, and neither the split form nor the pack's diagonal is ever called a stand-in for the release's covariance (section 10.6 of that document). Leg K1 tests the arithmetic of the product on a labelled synthetic factor and nothing else.
combination.syntheticFactor: chi2_other(Om) = ((Om - 0.28) / 0.03)^2, a labelled design factor that is NOT any survey's likelihood and has no supernova in it.

syntheticEnsemble.uncertainty: fractional sigma 2.0 percent on D_M/r_d and 4.0 percent on D_H/r_d at each redshift, correlation -0.4 between D_M/r_d and D_H/r_d at the same redshift (a design sign), zero between redshifts; sigma is a fraction of the TRUE value of the ratio.
syntheticEnsemble.coverageRule: a draw covers when the true Om lies in the (possibly grid-edge-truncated) set; the rate is judged against the nominal level p by p +- 3 sqrt(p (1 - p) / draws): [0.6515, 0.7139] at 68.27 percent, [0.9406, 0.9684] at 95.45 percent

demonstration.label: Optional correlation-function demonstration on the pack's galaxies: a pair-count script, Landy-Szalay (1993) estimator, a random catalog on 149's streams, a 157 grid; whether its BAO peak is detectable at the pack's size.
demonstration.sample: tests-visible pack data-packs/sdss-dr18-redshift-slice.json and its sidecar cosmology/sdss-dr18-redshift-slice.json: 2,911 galaxies, columns ra (1e-4 degree) and z; NO declination is stored. Declination is set to the strip's midpoint, 0.25 degree, for every galaxy and every random point (stated assumption; a pair's transverse separation is wrong by at most 0.5 degree x its distance, about 3.5 Mpc at 400 Mpc), and the footprint is the strip RA 120 to 240 degrees.
demonstration.fiducial: flat Lambda-CDM Om 0.3, H0 70 (h = 0.7), the lessons' stated wedge cosmology; separations in Mpc/h = h x Mpc. The sample's comoving distance uses the 255 kernel (prototype) and astropy (oracle).
demonstration.randoms: 10 x 2,911 = 29,110 points: RA = 120 + 120 u1 (degrees), z = the data's z at index floor(u2 Nd) (the shuffled-redshift method, a stated design choice: it removes the radial structure of the data from the random catalog), declination 0.25 degree; draws in pairs (u1, u2) in order from stream('injection', '257:bao:randoms') on mulberry32, seed text normalised by FNV-1a (js/rng.js). The oracle re-implements the published mulberry32 and the FNV-1a text rule and must reproduce the stream bit for bit (leg D1).
demonstration.estimator: xi(s) = (DD_n - 2 DR_n + RR_n) / RR_n with DD_n = DD / (Nd (Nd - 1) / 2), DR_n = DR / (Nd Nr), RR_n = RR / (Nr (Nr - 1) / 2), unordered pairs, 12 bins of 10 Mpc/h from 40 to 160 [lo, hi).
demonstration.jackknife: 12 blocks of 10 degrees of RA from 120; delete-one; sigma^2 = (12 - 1) / 12 sum (xi_k - mean)^2; randoms assigned to blocks by RA like the data; replicates from block-pair count matrices.
demonstration.detectabilityRule: smooth model: weighted straight line xi = alpha + beta log10 s fitted with weights 1 / sigma_jk^2 to the 8 bins OUTSIDE the peak window [90, 130) Mpc/h; S/N of a window bin = (xi - smooth) / sigma_jk; the peak is DETECTABLE iff the largest S/N over the 4 window bins is at least 4 (a Bonferroni-style threshold for four trials, stated). A bin whose RR is zero or whose sigma_jk is zero or not finite makes the leg refused (fails).
demonstration.nullEnsemble: 16 null data catalogs of 2,911 points built exactly like the randoms (seeds '257:bao:null:0' to '257:bao:null:15'), each measured against the SAME random catalog: no clustering by construction; per bin the mean xi over the 16 and sd / sqrt(16); the bound is |mean| <= 3 sd_mean + 0.001 in at least 11 of the 12 bins.
demonstration.bigPicture: A BAO peak is expected near the sound horizon (about 100 Mpc/h in an order-of-magnitude statement not used for any bound). The demonstration does not need r_d to be judged detectable; whether a measured peak position agrees with r_d needs F1 and is NOT RUN.

publishedComparison.label: Leg P1: the integral against a published full (Boltzmann-code) calculation, using ONLY what the printed table of the saved extracted text of arXiv:1807.06209 states, read after this file was committed, by a script that prints each line it used.
publishedComparison.source: Table 1 of the paper, the best-fit column of the first (Plik) data combination: the physical baryon density omegaB, the physical cold-dark-matter density omegaC, H0, the drag redshift z_drag and the sound horizon at the drag epoch r_drag, each with its printed digits, and the table's note on the neutrino mass. If the extraction is ambiguous for any of the five numbers, or the neutrino mass is not stated, the leg is NOT RUN (never a guess).
publishedComparison.model: flat (Ode = 1 - Om - Or), w = -1, T = 2.7255 K, Neff = 3.046, z_d = the printed z_drag, h = H0/100
publishedComparison.bracket: two cases bound the neutrino treatment this gate does not model: L: three massless species, Om = (omegaB + omegaC)/h^2, Or h^2 = omegaGamma (1 + 0.2271 x 3.046); H: one species of the stated mass as non-relativistic matter at z_d, Om = (omegaB + omegaC + omegaNu)/h^2 with omegaNu = (sum m_nu / 93.14 eV), Or h^2 = omegaGamma (1 + 0.2271 x 3.046 x 2/3). The two integrals give r_L and r_H; r_lo = min, r_hi = max.
publishedComparison.tolerance: u = one unit of the last printed digit of r_drag + the worst-case propagation of half a unit of the last printed digit of each of omegaB, omegaC, H0 and z_drag, by central finite differences of the integral (relative step 1e-4).
publishedComparison.reported: the position of r_drag between r_lo and r_hi as a fraction, and the distance outside the interval in units of u; never a pass criterion.
publishedComparison.limits: The leg tests the integral given z_drag, not z_drag; the neutrino bracket is one-sided honest about what is not modelled and is not a precision claim; 93.14 eV is the conventional constant of omega_nu h^2 = sum m / 93.14 eV.

ensemble.rule: numpy default_rng(257); each draw has H0 U(-20, 120), Om U(-0.1, 1.2), Ode 'flat' with probability 0.7 else U(0, 1.2), w U(-3.5, 0.5), Or U(-1e-5, 2e-4), omegaGamma U(-1e-6, 3e-5), omegaB U(-0.005, 0.03), zd U(-100, 12000); the oracle's brute-force decision (finite; the 255 bounds; E^2(x) > 0 on a log grid of 400,001 points for x in [1, 1e8]; the three new rules) in the order of soundHorizon.refusalCodesInOrder is the reference; the prototype must agree on accept/refuse and on the code for every draw, and on the sound horizon of every accepted draw to 1e-9 relative to the oracle's own quad.

verdict.rows: A leg with a group other than 'reported' and no 'expected: not-run' passes or fails by its bound; a leg with 'expected: not-run' is NOT RUN until its request is met; P1 is NOT RUN if its extraction is ambiguous; D6 decides only whether the demonstration is built and is never part of the ruler verdict. A pass/fail leg that cannot be measured fails the gate on that threshold.
verdict.kernel: KERNEL PASS iff every leg of groups integrity, ruler, ensemble, combination and refusals passes, P1 passes or is NOT RUN, and the demonstration's D1 to D5 pass if the demonstration is to be built; otherwise KERNEL FAIL.
verdict.A: KERNEL PASS and F1 to F5 pass and O1 to O3 pass: the ruler with the named observable (and the combined contours only if 256's committed verdict is not C, which today it is, so they are omitted), and the demonstration when D6 passes and D1 to D5 pass.
verdict.B: KERNEL PASS and F1 to F5 pass, and some O leg is NOT RUN or fails: the ruler only (Appendix C's B): the standard-ruler relation and a sound horizon with its cited formula and domain; never a named observable.
verdict.C: KERNEL FAIL, or any F leg that ran fails: a reading step; 260's The pillars omits BAO (Appendix C).
verdict.notEstablished: KERNEL PASS and some F leg NOT RUN (and no F leg failing): the verdict is NOT ESTABLISHED. It is neither A, B nor C: the ruler's cited fitting formula and its error against a full calculation have not been tested, and a B would claim them. The kernel's integral and relation are reported as passing or failing on their own legs.
verdict.consumersClause: met iff the verdict is A or B. NOT ESTABLISHED, C and a KERNEL FAIL do not meet it. Whatever the verdict, no panel, lesson, viewer or contour is built until Carl lifts the consumers rule.
verdict.partB: after A or B, and only after Carl goes ahead; not begun in this session.

amendments.recorded: after the saved text of arXiv:1807.06209 was searched for the lines the P1 rule names, and before the integral was run on any printed input, before the validator was run and before any result existed
amendments.what: P1 is judged NOT RUN as committed: its rule requires z_drag in the best-fit column of Table 1, and that column does not print it (Table 1's rows are omegaB, omegaC, 100 theta_MC, tau, ln(10^10 A_s), n_s, Omega_m h^2, H0, Omega_m, Age, sigma_8, S_8, z_re, 100 theta_*, r_drag; z_drag is a row of the paper's Table 2, whose columns are data combinations and marginalised means). A NEW leg P1b.plankRdragT2 is added with its bound committed here: the same rule as publishedComparison (the two-case neutrino bracket, the same model, the same tolerance terms) with the inputs omegaB, omegaC, H0 and r_drag from the BEST-FIT column of Table 1 and z_drag from the fifth numerical column of Table 2 (the column of the combination Planck TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing, the same combination as Table 1), a marginalised mean, so u gets one further term: |d r / d z_drag| x (sigma_z + half a unit of the last printed digit of z_drag), with sigma_z the printed uncertainty of that entry and the derivative taken as the larger of the two cases'. The pass rule is unchanged: r_drag printed in [r_lo - u, r_hi + u]. If the extraction is ambiguous, or a column header cannot be read from the saved text, P1b is NOT RUN. The kernel part of the verdict function reads P1b where it read P1: P1b passes or is NOT RUN; a failing P1b is a KERNEL FAIL.
amendments.seen: lines 1118 to 1230 of the saved text were printed while deciding (Table 1 and the Table 2 rows near z_drag); the printed numbers were therefore SEEN before this amendment, so P1b is NOT blind. No sound horizon was computed at any of them; the rule's terms are the committed ones and none was chosen from a printed value.
amendments.moves: no committed bound; P1 stays NOT RUN with the reason stated; one leg added with its bound committed before its first run

decisions.what: The named observable is committed as a form and a request, not as a release: no release, effective redshift, value or covariance of any survey is named, because each is published data and the instruction in force is that this session neither fetches nor types published data.
decisions.consequence: Legs O1 to O3 are NOT RUN; no B or A can be reached while they are, and B also needs F1 to F5.

decisions.what: No fitting formula for z_d or r_d is implemented: the coefficients are published numbers. The gate's ruler is the sound-horizon integral with z_d as an input; the cited formulas are legs F1 to F5, NOT RUN with an exact request (F1).
decisions.consequence: The product verdict cannot be better than NOT ESTABLISHED in this session.

decisions.what: Combination with 256: omitted, because 256's committed verdict is FC (Appendix C: 257's combination omitted); the product-of-likelihoods rule is stated and its arithmetic tested on a labelled synthetic factor that is not a supernova likelihood.
decisions.consequence: No joint contour with supernovae exists or is claimed.

decisions.what: The demonstration's declination is set to the strip's midpoint because the pack stores none; this is stated as a limitation of the pack, not of the estimator, and a production script would need a pack carrying declination (a data decision for Carl).
decisions.consequence: A detectability verdict here is a verdict about THIS pack with that assumption.
